## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dc29936fcbbfe9a6a5419b9be6ee0aa6b68b8c05`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/release.yml + none

Read: card #37587 with all four comments, PR #38119 (body, file list, net diff against `447757d0`, +25/−0 in one file), and the 48 check-runs on the head (30 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed). The tree was read at the head with `git show`; nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of the version job: one more content gate. Right.** `run_gate pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec --fail-if-no-match exec vitest run --project local scripts/build-migration-registry-entry.test.ts` sits after the `protocol-version.test.ts` line and has the same shape. A post-version tree with no `os-generated` region for the spec package's major or for `PROTOCOL_MAJOR`, in any of the three kinds, now fails "Validate the post-version tree". The Version PR step does not run, and the standing PR keeps its last validated content.
- **The filter selects the file. Right.** `packages/spec/vitest.config.ts` gives `local` the include `scripts/**/*.test.ts` minus `vitest.repo-tests.json`, and that list does not name this file. `pnpm --filter … exec` runs in `packages/spec`, so the relative path resolves. A renamed or moved file selects nothing, and vitest exits non-zero, so the gate cannot go green on an empty run.
- **It runs in the job's state (install, no build). Right, by reading.** The test imports `scripts/build-migration-registry.ts` (node builtins only, behind an entry guard) and `src/kernel/protocol-version.ts` (no imports). It spawns `packages/spec/node_modules/.bin/tsx`, which the install provides. It does not read the generated `registry.ts`. The config's preflight import is a source path, and the adjacent `protocol-version.test.ts` gate already loads it in this job.
- **It leaves the tree as it found it. Right.** The three spawned runs are `--self-test` (exits before the write) and an import probe. The files it writes are under `os.tmpdir()`. The moved-path list is captured in the step before, so nothing here can enter the Version PR.
- **Public surface: none.** No package, schema, script or trigger changes. The job stays `schedule` / `workflow_dispatch` only.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no

`skip-changeset` is right: the diff is a workflow file and publishes nothing. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in os-dev-report 7232717040: empty. `out_of_scope_findings`: empty.
- Deviation (the head branch was pushed as a new branch after the queue deleted it): no effect on the diff. One commit on `447757d0`.
- No check-run on this head runs the changed step, because the job never runs on a pull request. The first live run is the next scheduled refresh after merge. The evidence that the command runs there is the reading in ① plus the dev's measurement (7 passed, 2.2 s; ablation red naming the region). A failure there is loud and leaves the Version PR stale, never broken.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff holds no query.
- Tier H by path: landing needs an authorized approval. This record does not replace it.

### ④ Design judgment

`.github/workflows/release.yml`, against the card's item 1 and the code it cites.

- **It pins what the card asks for.** Item 1 expects "the version pass runs the region pin, or the three tests, before it opens the Version PR". The pin reads the spec major from `packages/spec/package.json`, which the version pass has just rewritten, and `PROTOCOL_MAJOR`, which `sync-protocol-version.mjs` moves in the same pass. It then requires an opened and closed region per kind for both. That is the #37549 defect (`retired-key:19` missing while the package's major was 19), widened to all three kinds.
- **The header's account of when it bites is true.** On a boundary train the moved `protocol-version.ts` is collected into `UNVALIDATED`, not exited on, so every `run_gate` still runs and both verdicts land in one run. `run_gate` records the whole command line in `failed`, so the final error names the test file. The assertion text names the region and both majors.
- **The three exclusions hold against the tree.**
  - Retired-keys check-mode test: it is in `vitest.repo-tests.json` (the `repo` project). Its red on the 19 tree was the generator refusing `19.*` entries for want of the region (#37549), which the pin judges without running the generator.
  - Runtime `mcp-authoring.test.ts`: it imports `@objectstack/objectql`, `driver-sql`, `metadata` and `metadata-protocol`. `packages/runtime/vitest.config.ts` has no alias for objectql, and that package's `exports` point at `dist`. It needs a build.
  - ui `doc-version-claims.test.ts`: its only input the version pass moves is the spec major, used to key the `skills/objectui/SKILL.md` pin claim. `check:skill-compatibility` judges that pin against the same manifest and runs earlier in this list. Its scan roots hold no CHANGELOG and no other stamped file.
- **`Fixes #37587` is right.** Item 1 is this PR. Item 2: `mcp-authoring.ts:232` builds the example from `specVersionExample(server)`, landed by #37821 (merged, `5e1d58a0`). Item 3: the module-top read is `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('@objectstack/spec/package.json')`, landed by #38089 (merged, `447757d0`, the base of this head).

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (prose only, in the header comment):

- N1 (nit) — "pin check:skill-compatibility already judges above": the WHAT IS CHECKED list has no `check:skill-compatibility` entry. "Above" is true only of the `run_gate` order, 300 lines further down.
- N2 (nit) — "judged here by this pin structurally, at 132 s": the time belongs to the excluded retired-keys test, but it reads as the pin's, five lines after "2.3 s measured".
- N3 (nit) — the header says 2.3 s; the PR body and the os-dev-report say 2.2 s. The list's opening totals ("7 s total", "44 s") predate this gate and are not restated.

## Contract review brief — PR #38119 @ `dc29936fcbbfe9a6a5419b9be6ee0aa6b68b8c05` (card #37587)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths .github/workflows/release.yml` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37587: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #38119: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `dc29936fcbbfe9a6a5419b9be6ee0aa6b68b8c05`
  · the check-runs on `dc29936fcbbfe9a6a5419b9be6ee0aa6b68b8c05`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: .github/workflows/release.yml;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-38119/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.

- **风险**：只在校验步骤里加一行检查和一段注释，不碰发布、打 tag 或部署。误报的话，版本 PR 只是暂时不刷新，撤回这一行就恢复。
